title: watchDeployment
summary: Recover stale production navigation without adding code to the core router.

sections.title: Parameters
sections.body: Pass a Smolter navigation or data router and DeploymentOptions from virtual:smolter/deployment. Null metadata is a no-op for development and SSR. Install once before starting a manual router or creating its fetchers, or pass deployment metadata directly to mountApplication so recovery also covers the initial route import.

sections.title: Result and disposal
sections.body: Returns a cleanup function. Cleanup removes the popstate and Vite listeners, aborts a pending manifest request and restores router methods. router.dispose() also calls cleanup.

sections.title: Navigation behavior
sections.body: Pathname/query navigation and Back/Forward compare destination dependencies and shared application fingerprints. Unrelated route changes keep client navigation. Changed shared code, changed/missing destinations, or missing compatibility metadata require document recovery. Successful routine checks are reused for 30 seconds (checkInterval); chunk failures bypass this cache. Hash-only/external links skip checks. Concurrent checks share a request; only the latest intent may reload. Mutations are never replayed.

sections.title: Failures and cache policy
sections.body: Network errors, bad JSON and timeouts fall back to normal navigation. A session marker limits recovery to one reload per old build/manifest URL. Blocked storage disables automatic reload. Serve the manifest with no-store and HTML with no-cache. A custom reload callback owns confirmation/navigation and receives the destination URL. Idle intent-prefetch failures do not reload the current page or consume the recovery marker. Recovery waits for navigation to record a destination; overlapping checks honor the newest navigation. New history operations invalidate pending checks even when returning to the current route. Starting a mutation cancels earlier recovery checks. Redirect chunk recovery uses the committed router URL, including query and hash, rather than the URL of the original click.
